name: Zombie to New York
summary: The bottom Zombie player completes the contested hand-clearing action, places the hand on the mat, and establishes the knee hug that defines completed New York control.
description: The bottom Zombie player completes the contested hand-clearing action, places the hand on the mat, and establishes the knee hug that defines completed New York control.
overview:
The bottom Zombie player completes the contested hand-clearing action, places the hand on the mat, and establishes the knee hug that defines completed New York control.

Begin in the Zombie hand-clearing checkpoint, before completed New York control has been secured. Retain the first high-leg connection while the opposing hand is being cleared.

Complete the hand-clearing action rather than treating a partially displaced hand as success. Establish the knee-hug connection after the hand reaches the mat. The destination is New York/Bottom only after both the hand-to-mat and knee-hug checkpoints exist. If the hand-clearing connection is lost, recognize the retained Mission Control configuration before starting again.

Practice cooperatively with controlled movement. Stop at any tap, verbal signal, or distress; release all joint or neck pressure before changing direction. Do not force a trapped knee, shoulder, or neck to preserve the route.

defender.name: Zombie to New York Defender
defender.description: Recognize Zombie to New York and interrupt its required connections before the final control is established.
defender.overview:
You oppose the performer of this action. Keep the hand connected to useful inside space while the pummel is contested. Address the hand clearance before the knee hug closes. Maintain a balanced posture without forcing the raised knee. Recognize an unfinished pummel as Zombie rather than completed New York. Rebuild inside hand position if the holder returns to Mission Control.

Practice cooperatively with controlled movement. Stop at any tap, verbal signal, or distress; release all joint or neck pressure before changing direction. Do not force a trapped knee, shoulder, or neck to preserve the route.

flashcards.question: Against Zombie to New York, does interrupting one grip guarantee a new position?
